en.name: Saint Bartholomew, Apostle
en.summary: Honors one of the Twelve Apostles, widely identified with Nathanael and traditionally martyred by flaying.
en.body: This feast honors Bartholomew, one of the Twelve Apostles who many scholars and long-standing tradition identify with Nathanael, the skeptical friend of Philip whom John's Gospel describes Jesus praising as "an Israelite in whom there is no deceit" upon their first meeting. Beyond his inclusion in the apostolic lists, little is recorded of him with certainty in Scripture, but strong tradition holds he carried the Gospel to Armenia and other regions of the ancient Near East, and that he was martyred by being flayed alive, an ordeal that made him a frequent subject in Christian art, often depicted holding his own skin, most famously in Michelangelo's Sistine Chapel Last Judgment. His relics are venerated in Rome at the Basilica of San Bartolomeo all'Isola.
